subject: POC: Trial environment options and next steps (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir.rao@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@brighthealth.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: POC: Trial environment options and next steps (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC)

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we’re aligned before we kick off the POC.

High-level goal (what success looks like)
- Reduce inference latency for our triage microservice from ~450ms to <200ms at 95th percentile for 2k rps production-like load
- Maintain prediction quality within +/- 2% of baseline (we’ll use the shared eval set)
- Demonstrate predictable per-request cost under the target throughput

Technical constraints / must-haves you mentioned
- Data residency: all PII must remain in-us (we should validate region placement)
- KMS integration for key management
- Network allowlisting (BrightHealth firewall)

POC options for environment (brief)
1) Hosted Redwood API (fastest): Redwood hosted endpoints in us-west with dedicated project space. Quickest to start (1–2 business days), limited control over network egress IPs, KMS via customer-managed key (where supported).
2) Dedicated sandbox (recommended for this POC): Reserved GPU pool that we provision for the trial with isolated tenancy and stable IPs for allowlisting. SLA-like behavior for the length of the trial. Spin-up ~3–5 business days.
3) VPC trial (private deployment): On-prem/VPC-connected deployment for full network control and air-gapped option. Longer lead time (2–4 weeks) and requires infra coordination.

Proposed success criteria / evaluation plan
- Week 0: Kickoff and environment selection, exchange sample eval data + allowlist IPs
- Week 1: Environment provisioning + baseline run on your eval set
- Week 2: Optimization (batching, quantization profile) and perf re-test
- Week 3: Final validation and handoff + cost/ops review

Ownership / next steps
- Marissa (me): POC project manager, schedule demos and weekly syncs
- Dev Patel (cc’d): technical lead for environment setup and model onboarding
- BrightHealth: provide eval dataset (anonymized) and network contacts for allowlist

Attachments: POC-plan.xlsx (high-level timeline + checklist), trial-env-options.pdf (deltas between environments)

Question for you: which environment do you want us to provision for the trial (Hosted / Dedicated sandbox / VPC)? If Dedicated, please confirm target region (us-west/us-east) and list of firewall IPs to allow.

If you’re good with this plan, I’ll get Dev looped in to start provisioning and we’ll send a calendar invite for kickoff.

Thanks,
Marissa
--
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

We’ll get the anonymized eval set to you by end of day Friday. Elena — any concerns on your side?

Subject: Re: POC: Trial environment options and next steps (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC)

Hi all — quick technical note on environment differences and lead times: 

- Hosted Redwood API:
  * Lead time: same-day to 2 business days to provision project and API keys
  * KMS: we support customer-managed keys for token storage and persistent artifacts in the hosted product (we’ll need a key ARN and IAM role to access)
  * IPs: Hosted endpoints use dynamic egress ranges; we can provide a published list but cannot guarantee single static IPs per customer
  * Best for rapid validation and early perf baselines

- Dedicated sandbox (recommended):
  * Lead time: typically 3 business days if capacity is available; 5 business days if we need to allocate GPUs from regional pools
  * KMS: full CMK support and ability to disable persistent logs to meet compliance needs
  * IPs: we can provision a small set of static egress IPs for allowlisting
  * Network: require BrightHealth to allow outbound to those IPs and open ports 443; we can provide an allowlist template (attached)

- VPC trial (private deployment):
  * Lead time: 2–4 weeks (depends on cloud infra and customer network ops)
  * KMS: uses customer KMS inside VPC or HSM integration where required
  * Use-case: required when full network isolation or air-gapped testing is needed

Notes / action items for BrightHealth engineers:
- Send anonymized eval set (S3 link or secure upload)
- Provide target region (us-west/us-east) and allowlist IPs (we’ll respond with ours)
- If you need dedicated GPUs, tell us expected peak RPS and sequence lengths so we can size the sandbox

Attached: network-allowlist-template.txt

Happy to start provisioning Dedicated sandbox as soon as I get confirmation on region and an estimate for peak RPS.

\u0014 Dev
Dev Patel
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai
[Attachment: network-allowlist-template.txt]

1) Can you guarantee static egress IPs for the duration of the trial? We need to add them to our firewall with at least a 7-day lead time.
2) Please confirm CMK/KMS workflow and whether we need to supply IAM permissions up front or you’ll provide a role we can assume.

We’ll provide the anonymized eval set today (S3 link to follow) and a rough traffic profile: 2k rps peak, average payloads ~1.2k tokens, occasional long jobs ~6k tokens. If you need any other sizing info, let us know.

Elena
